document_title: Wheat (Kanak/Gehun) advisory from PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26

sections.section_title: Yellow Rust (Pila Rataua / Peeli Kungi) Identification and Management
sections.symptoms: Yellow powdery pustules in stripes on the leaves; the yellow powder sticks to hands. It appears first in the sub-mountainous areas, in cool humid weather (7-13°C nights, 15-24°C days); rain with wind in February-March spreads it.
sections.recommended_action: Monitor the crop from the second week of December onward, especially after irrigation or rain. As soon as the disease is noticed, spray 200 ml Tilt/Bumper 25 EC (propiconazole) or 120 g Nativo 75 WG (trifloxystrobin + tebuconazole) or 300 g Taqat 75 WP (captan + hexaconazole) in 200 liters of water per acre. At first spray only the infected patches and around them. Keep monitoring and repeat the spray as needed.
sections.preventive_measures: Grow rust resistant varieties: PBW Biscuit 1, PBW Zinc 2, PBW RS1, PBW 725, Unnat PBW 550, PBW 752, WHD 943, PDW 291 and PBW 660. In the sub-mountainous zone, do not sow in October.
sections.critical_safety_warning: Do not spray fungicide during high wind velocity to avoid chemical drift. Always wear protective masks.
sections.source_reference: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26, pages 18-21

sections.section_title: Karnal Bunt (Tilletia indica) Management in Wheat
sections.symptoms: Only a few grains in a spike are partially transformed into a black powdery mass of teliospores. Crushed grains give an unpleasant rotten-fish odor due to trimethylamine.
sections.recommended_action: PAU recommends a single spray of 200 ml Tilt 25 EC (propiconazole) in 200 liters of water per acre at ear emergence only for wheat grown for seed, to produce Karnal bunt free seed. For wheat grown for grain, PAU does not recommend this spray: grow resistant varieties and use clean seed.
sections.preventive_measures: Grow the resistant varieties WHD 943 and PDW 291. Use clean, certified seed. In a seed crop, remove off-type and diseased plants at frequent intervals.
sections.source_reference: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26, pages 17 and 19-21

sections.section_title: Wheat Sowing Time, Seed Rate, and Critical Irrigation Stages
sections.recommended_action: The first fortnight of November is the best sowing time for wheat; long-duration varieties can be sown from the fourth week of October. Each week of delay cuts yield by about 150 kg per acre. Seed rate is 40 kg per acre (45 kg for PBW 869 and Unnat PBW 550; 45 kg with a Happy Seeder). Fertilizer on medium soils: 55 kg DAP at sowing, then 45 kg urea per acre with each of the first two irrigations.
sections.preventive_measures: Give a heavy pre-sowing irrigation, except after rice. Give the first irrigation, a light one, 3 weeks after sowing for October-sown wheat and 4 weeks after sowing for later sowing.
sections.source_reference: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26, pages 4-6, 9-11 and 16-17

sections.symptoms: Small green insects clustering on leaves and earheads during February-March. They suck sap, resulting in shrivelled grain and reduced yield.
sections.recommended_action: Spray only if aphids exceed the economic threshold of 5 aphids per earhead (count 10 random earheads in each of the 4 quarters of one acre). Give two sprays of 2 liters PAU homemade neem extract at a weekly interval, or a single spray of 20 g Actara/Taiyo 25 WG (thiamethoxam) in 80-100 liters of water per acre with a knapsack sprayer (30 liters of water with a power sprayer). Apply insecticide only if aphids attack at the earhead stage.
sections.preventive_measures: Aphids appear first on the field borders, so spray only the infested strip. Spraying only above the threshold also spares ladybird beetles and other natural enemies.
sections.source_reference: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Rabi 2025-26, page 17
